hints.S55_A1: The kitten DID NOT STRUGGLE AT ALL, and it is compared to a FEATHER. Ask: is a feather rough and loud, or soft and calm? Match the adjective to the feather, not to the weight of the animal.
hints.S55_A2: The diver is EXPERIENCED and finished the whole mission IN UNDER TWENTY MINUTES. Ask: does the idiom describe something very easy, or something very hard? An idiom cannot be read word by word - it is not about food.
hints.S55_A3: The eagle is INJURED and must be kept UNTIL ITS WING HEALED COMPLETELY. Ask: which phrasal verb means to look after a creature that needs help? 'Release' would send it away while it is still hurt.
hints.S55_A4: The team is AVOIDING ANY SUDDEN MOVEMENTS THAT MIGHT SCARE THE TRAPPED ANIMAL. Ask: which noun names great watchfulness taken to avoid harm? 'Speed', 'noise' and 'strength' would frighten the animal even more.
hints.S55_A5: The centre gives the flooded animals FOOD, WATER AND A DRY PLACE TO SLEEP. Ask: which word names a temporary place of safety? A 'market' sells things and a 'school' teaches children.
hints.S55_B1: The subject is ANYONE - one person at a time, no matter how big the crowd on the road. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb with -s? The long WHO clause changes nothing.
hints.S55_B2: OVER FIVE HUNDRED DOLLARS is in the fund now, and HAS is already in place. Ask: after 'has', which form builds a present perfect? This verb is regular, so it takes the ordinary ending.
hints.S55_B3: THAN IT WAS ... THREE WEEKS AGO measures the turtle against its own past - just two states. Ask: does a short adjective ending in -y take an ending of its own, or the word 'most'? 'Most' is for three or more.
hints.S55_B4: THE RESCUE COORDINATOR CALLED THEM BACK - one sharp event interrupting a longer one. Ask: which choice shows the volunteers halfway through the job at that moment? A plain past verb tells you it was already finished.
hints.S55_B5: THE VET COULD NOT TELL WHAT HAD HAPPENED, so the amount of INFORMATION was small - and information can never be counted. Ask: which quantity word means 'not much' and partners an uncountable noun?
hints.S55_B6: The verb of the statement is WAS - 'the operation WAS the most dangerous mission'. Ask: after a positive statement, is the tag positive or negative? The tag must copy that same verb, never invent a new one.
hints.S55_B7: The PANGOLIN is injured and helpless - A TEAM OF TRAINED VOLUNTEERS did the moving LAST FRIDAY. Ask: which choice makes the subject the receiver of the action, and places it in the past?
hints.S55_B8: A reported command with a safety reason: WITHOUT PROPER GLOVES OR PROTECTIVE GEAR. Ask: after 'told + person', is it the plain verb, the -ing form, or 'to' + verb? And where does the negative word sit?
hints.S55_C1: The otter is measured against A CHAMPION SWIMMER, and neither of them wins. Ask: which box phrase shows two things moving at exactly the same speed? An '-er than' phrase would make one of them quicker.
hints.S55_C2: OF ALL THE ANIMALS AT OUR CENTRE - that is many, not a pair - and the loris FITS IN THE PALM OF ONE HAND. Ask: which box phrase is a superlative, the one that beats every other animal there?
hints.S55_C3: Exactly two lizards are set against each other: the ADULT MONITOR LIZARD and THE YOUNG ONE rescued last month. Ask: which box phrase compares two things unequally, using the -er ending? A superlative needs three or several.
hints.S55_C4: AFTER A WEEK WITHOUT FOOD the eagle has lost its power, so it falls short of A HEALTHY WILD EAGLE. Ask: which box phrase says one thing does NOT reach the level of another? It is the negative twin of the 'as ... as' pattern.
hints.S55_C5: The clue is WEIGHING ALMOST TWICE AS MUCH - not a small gap, but a huge one. Ask: which box phrase puts an intensifier in front of the comparative? Never say 'very' before a comparative form.
hints.S55_C6: Count the CIVETS in that sentence: a pair arrived, and one of them is called THE SMALLER ONE. Ask: which box phrase picks out the other member of a pair? A superlative would need at least three animals.
hints.S55_C7: WITHOUT TREATMENT, the animal did not simply get worse once - it kept sliding downhill UNTIL THE VET ARRIVED. Ask: which box phrase repeats a comparative to show a change going on step by step?
hints.S55_C8: Read the ending: the mission OUR TEAM HAS EVER FACED - it is set against every mission in the team's whole history. Ask: which box phrase is a superlative built with a long adjective? Do not drop its little opening word.
hints.S55_D1: The dash explains it: TRAINED DOCTORS EXAMINE ITS WOUNDS. The blank sits in front of 'care', so it must say what kind of care. Ask: which box word means 'to do with the medical treatment of animals'?
hints.S55_D2: The dash defines it: EASILY HURT BY SUDDEN MOVEMENTS, which is why HANDLERS MUST STAY CALM. Ask: which box word means easily damaged? 'Ferocious' would put the handlers in danger, not the animal.
hints.S55_D3: The clue follows the comma: LEFT ALONE WITHOUT FOOD OR SHELTER by their owners. Ask: which box word means deserted and left to fend for itself? A 'poacher' is a person who hunts illegally.
hints.S55_D4: ONCE FULLY RECOVERED, the animal goes BACK INTO ITS NATURAL HABITAT. The blank follows 'will', so a base verb is needed. Ask: which box word means to set a creature free? 'Capture' does the exact opposite.
hints.S55_D5: The dash spells it out: A SAFE HAVEN FOR LIFE, for animals that CANNOT SURVIVE ALONE. Ask: which box word names a permanent place of refuge? 'A PERMANENT' in front of it proves the blank must be a noun.
hints.S55_E1: THE VOLUNTEERS is the subject of the underlined verb - a whole group of them. Ask: which past form of 'to be' belongs with a plural subject? The singular form can only serve one person or one thing.
hints.S55_E2: Stretch the underlined word out: 'you are GOING TO HELP' fits the sentence perfectly. Ask: when two words are squeezed into one, which mark shows the missing letter? The other spelling only shows possession.
hints.S55_E3: The mynah SNATCHED A BISCUIT FROM AN OPEN BAG, so the underlined word names a stealer - and its vowels are back to front. Ask: with no C in front, which vowel comes first, the I or the E?
hints.S55_E4: The underlined word is not describing the otter - it describes the manner in which she APPEARED FROM BEHIND THE REEDS. Ask: which class of word may modify a verb, and what ending does it usually carry?
hints.S55_E5: The REPORT was written by the whole team, so it belongs to more than one person. Ask: which mark turns a plural into a possessive, and does it sit before or after the -s that is standing there already?
hints.S55_F1: 'SINCE' introduces a fact that is ALREADY TRUE: the animal HAS BEEN SPOTTED near your home. Ask: which half is the reason, and which is the advice? Never put 'will' in the reason half; keep 'should' in the other.
hints.S55_F2: The VET's exact words were a yes/no question. Ask: which little joining word must follow ASKED? Does a reported question keep its question order, or take normal statement order? A past reporting verb pulls the tense back.
